So dairy farmers in Wisconsin work hard every day to make sure that their milk meets the high standards for nutritional value and quality that is in federal law. But we have seen an explosion of imitation products that have gotten away with using dairy's good name for their own benefit, which is actually against the

and that law must be enforced. So the Dairy Pride Act pushes the FDA, the Food and Drug Administration, to actually enforce the law because this labeling of plant-based products as milk really does hurt our dairy farmers and their hard work should be recognized and the law should be enforced.
The National Milk Producers Federation is strongly supporting the Dairy Pride Act and we should note that it has bipartisan support in both the Senate and the House, doesn't it?

It sure does and I have been pleased to join with Senator Risch in the United States Senate in reintroducing the Dairy Pride Act. So it is something that I think people who represent dairy farmers really understand the importance of seeing our federal standards for dairy enforced.

Well, the Food and Drug Administration oversees the part of federal law that defines what milk is and what nutritional value and quality it has to have. This wouldn't solve the problems that dairy farmers are facing because there's so many, but it would certainly be a step in the right direction And it was seen in the last two years alone, 1,200 small and medium sized family farms go out of business.
